source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
SJC29 publishes 40,000 square feet of technical space and no IT load figure in megawatts. Because no power number is published, no rack or accelerator estimate can be derived, and any such figure would be fabricated. At a common colocation density of 150 to 200 watts per square foot, 40,000 square feet would imply roughly 6 to 8 MW of IT load, but that is an assumption applied to a floor-area figure, not a number the operator has stated, and density varies widely across mixed-use colocation space.

The four certifications qualify the campus to host specific workload categories. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data environments. ISO 27001 qualifies it for tenants with formal information security management requirements. ISO 9001 qualifies it under a quality management framework. LEED indicates the building meets a recognized standard for energy and environmental design. None of these certifications identify actual tenants or confirm AI-specific infrastructure such as high-density power delivery or liquid cooling.

California has 103 mapped facilities in this site's dataset, of which only 5 have published a megawatt figure, totaling 170 MW across those five. SJC29 ranks sixth by published megawatts, which in practice means it falls outside the five facilities that contributed any number at all to that total. Silicon Valley land and power constraints are well documented in public reporting, but no specific grid or power data for this address is published in the operator's specification. For a reader assessing AI relevance, the absence of a power figure is the operative fact: compute capacity cannot be estimated from floor area alone, and this campus's contribution to AI workloads at scale cannot be determined from what is published.
